claims.claim: favorable habitat holds 0.4–0.8 beaver colonies per km²
claims.quote: The density of colonies in favorable habitat ranges from 0.4 to 0.8/km2
claims.conditions: '(1 to 2/mi2)'; a literature range compiled from Lawrence 1954, Aleksiuk 1968, Voigt et al. 1976 and Bergerud & Miller 1977 'cited by Jenkins and Busher 1979'; not Allen's own data and not specific to Maine or the Northeast
claims.note: Allen relays it from Jenkins & Busher 1979; 'Allen 1982, after Jenkins & Busher 1979' would be the honest form.

claims.claim: colonies are mostly on (favor) stream gradients under (below) 6 %
claims.location: p. 3 (PDF p. 10), Water; model text p. 9 (PDF p. 16)
claims.quote: colonies recorded in Colorado were in valleys with a stream gradient of less than 6%
claims.conditions: 68 % of the colonies recorded in Colorado (Retzer et al. 1956) were in valleys with stream gradient < 6 %, 28 % at 7–12 %, 4 % at 13–14 %, none at ≥ 15 %; the HSI model then gives 'Stream channel gradients of 6% or less' optimum value (p. 9, PDF p. 16). Riverine habitat only; marshes, ponds and lakes 'were nearly always occupied' when food was adequate
claims.note: 'Mostly' rests on one Colorado survey (68 %) relayed by Allen; the 6 % threshold is also the model's optimum. Fine as written; 'about two-thirds of colonies in a Colorado survey' would be more exact.

claims.claim: most beaver cutting is within 30 m of water
claims.quote: In a California study, 90% of all cutting of woody material was within 30 m
claims.conditions: '… (98.4 ft) of the water's edge (Hall 1970)'; also Jenkins (1980), Massachusetts: 'most of the trees utilized by beaver … were within 30 m', with some foraging to 100 m and reports to 200 m (Bradt 1938). The model (p. 9, PDF p. 16) treats woody food within 100 m as full value and beyond 200 m as none

notes: All three values hold in the September 1982 original; the only correction is the edition (the URL serves the 1982 original, not the 1983 revision). Other values in the report that may be useful for the beaver/wetland text: woody stems cut are usually < 7.6–10.1 cm dbh (p. 2, PDF p. 9); colonies need stable water and a channel gradient < 15 % (p. 4, PDF p. 11); mean distance between colonies 1.59 km in an Alaskan riverine habitat (Boyce 1981); subadults disperse in their second spring, on average 8–16 stream km (p. 4, PDF p. 11); minimum habitat assumed 0.8 km of stream channel or 1.3 km² of lake or marsh (p. 5, PDF p. 12); water-lily rhizomes can replace woody winter food (p. 2, PDF p. 9). The HSI model is explicitly 'a hypothesis of species-habitat relationships' (Preface, PDF p. 5).
